title: Hello, I'm BadCode: script options
about: This page lays out options for BadCode's spoken lines in 'Hello, I'm BadCode': ten writers' shapes ranked, and three combined drafts to pick from. Nothing has changed yet: no scene file, script or voice has been touched.

shapes.name: Comedy first
shapes.title: Comedy first, bluntness and bad timing deliver the facts

shapes.name: Reversal
shapes.title: Reversal, the viewer works out the point first

shapes.name: Borrowed craft
shapes.title: borrowed craft from trailers, cold opens and channel intros

dialogues.label: BadCode's lines (the whole short)
dialogues.where: hook 0-4 s over the warm opening; figure 4-7 s to camera; button on black after the reel, about 15-20 s
dialogues.target: about 8 seconds of speech in total across the three moments; the hook short enough to land in the first 2 seconds

drafts.name: Receipts
drafts.bet: The hook is a verdict, not a greeting, so the warm opening is a countdown; the figure introduces itself and hands the future back to the viewer in one word.

lines.line: Hello. I'm from the future. Yours.

notes: Trim: nothing; already under 8 s. Hold a beat of silence before 'Yours.' and keep the close-up still.
Protected line kept verbatim, nothing after it.

Risk: 'Yours.' dies on a flat read or a loose cut; 'Enjoy this. I checked.' can read as menace without warmth (casting). 'It went wrong' is never said, so the reel must carry it. All guesses until heard.

drafts.name: The good part
drafts.bet: The nostalgia is the last good thing, and BadCode names it on the cut, so the future going wrong is implied by one sentence and no disaster is mentioned.

lines.line: I'm from the future. [beat] That was the good part.

notes: Trim: if the voice runs slow, drop 'Hello.' from the hook; keep the stillness before 'That was the good part.'

Risk: could be heard as sneering at the nostalgia the viewer loves (voice.md: contempt at the mistake, never the people); delivery must be dry and warm. Keeps the plain 'from the future' that shape 01's 'from later' risked losing.

drafts.name: One place, one task
drafts.bet: A single concrete image of the future plus a task makes the case: the car park under the sea says it went wrong, and 'homework' makes the button a promise being collected.

lines.line: Where I'm from, the car park is the sea. [beat] I came back with homework.
[a full second of nothing] Here's what to do next.

notes: Trim: the figure line runs about 1.4 s past the 4-7 s window; if the cut is tight drop 'I came back with homework' (then ~6.6 s).
Protected line kept verbatim; only a silence is added before it.

Risk: 'car park' is British (swap 'parking lot' for a US audience) and is a climate-only image; 'future' is never said so a cold viewer may read it as a weather joke; 'homework' may sound childish and soften the reel.

ranking.verdict: Best fit. Hook is a finished fact that works muted; 'Yours.' puts the premise on the viewer without stating a moral; protected line untouched. Fails: 'Yours.' lives or dies on delivery; 'went wrong' only implied.
'That was the good part.' is the sharpest turn on the cut and says everything unstated. Fails: 'from later' may read as a typo; 3 s under target; no nurture before the button.
'Enjoy this' is the best hook and the silence does the writing. Fails: far under target; never says the future went wrong; generic sci-fi teaser if the reel is skipped.
Homework makes the button a payoff. Fails: keeps 'It didn't go well', the line Kai called basic; hook 3.4 s misses the 2 s landing; 'doing lovely' crowds the cut.
Withholding is right and 'Look' hands over to the reel. Fails: nothing says future; a cold viewer gets a creepy wellness line.
Specific and funny, only BadCode would say it. Fails: climate-only, British, 'future' never said; a cold viewer may hear weather small talk.
Quotable and caption-ready. Fails: 'Spoiler' and 'I'm the patch' are glib and dating, close to the 'BadCode wouldn't say that' note; 'patch' states the moral.
Bad timing as a joke is on voice. Fails: 'Sorry' risks flippancy about real suffering; 'I'm here to fix that' states the promise aloud; 'Don't get comfortable' is a trailer growl.
Customer-service calm is a clear character. Fails: 'Apologies for any inconvenience' mocks people who suffer, not the mistake; reads as a brand joke.
Fails hardest: 'Therefore, it went wrong' states the point the reel should make; no sarcasm, cold, essay voice.

questions.text: Should the figure say 'from the future' in words (1A, 1B), or should the viewer infer it (1C, shape 06)? A cold viewer on a trailer may need the plain phrase.
Is 'It didn't go well.' fully retired? Kai called it basic; only shape 10 kept it, and no draft here does.
Is about 6 s of speech acceptable against the 8 s target, or do you want more voice (1C reaches 8 s)?
Is a spoken hook that tells people to enjoy the warm opening ('Enjoy this') right, or does it sneer at the nostalgia people love? It depends on the voice cast.
Should the full second of silence before 'Here's what to do next.' be written in the script (1C) or left to the edit?
